discovery: Prediction and discovery of kilonovae: radioactively powered transients from neutron-star mergers that forge the heaviest elements

nominees.name: Brian D. Metzger
nominees.affiliation: Columbia University and Flatiron Institute, USA

subfield: Astrophysics: time-domain and multi-messenger astronomy, nuclear astrophysics
motivation: Where the heaviest elements such as gold, platinum and uranium come from was one of the great open questions in physics. Metzger and collaborators (2010) worked out that r-process nucleosynthesis in the neutron-rich ejecta of neutron-star mergers powers a distinctive thermal transient, the kilonova, and predicted its luminosity and timescale. Kasen's radiative-transfer calculations showed that lanthanide opacities make kilonovae red and infrared, which set how to search for them. Tanvir led the first detection of a kilonova, with Hubble in the infrared afterglow of the short gamma-ray burst GRB 130603B (2013). This framework was confirmed spectacularly in 2017, when the counterpart of the gravitational-wave event GW170817 matched the predictions. Together, this work links nuclear physics, gravitational waves and gamma-ray bursts, establishes neutron-star mergers as major cosmic sites of r-process elements, and opens multi-messenger astrophysics as a precision laboratory.
